learnings.summary: Reduced cache capacity regressed rotating-history p95; preserve original cache default and reject the side-panel experiment.
Keep initial index cost separate from reused-index results; measurements from an earlier helper and uncontrolled disk cache do not establish final package or UI performance.

notes.status: Code review found no additional concrete deployment defects; release acceptance remains conditional on the pending build and installation evidence.
reviewed: build-native.ps1 builds both locked Cargo manifests, copies the helper and Node addon, then hashes their bytes into native/manifest.json using native-hash.ps1.
run-release-build.ps1 records native Tauri exit status in target/release-build-result.json; ensure the root target directory exists before launching this wrapper.
Tauri resources include desktop/native and native, and desktop package/config versions both read 0.2.5. verify-desktop-binary.ps1 validates ProductVersion and outputs SHA256.

deploy-performance.py checks native and Advisor payload hashes, guards the verified kernel and Advisor version, validates destination containment, backs up previous bytes and installs the desktop executable last.
The Advisor deployment manifest names exactly index.js, observer.js and turn-tracker.js; the rejected side-panel experiment is excluded.

Install and rollback image-rename intent is journaled before rename. Recovery validates the expected sibling name, roots and SHA256 before restoring. The nine reported passing deployment tests were inspected, not rerun.
checklist: Record the exact reviewed source revision and working-tree state, require release-build-result.json exitCode=0, and preserve full build output.
Verify the executable ProductVersion is 0.2.5 and record its SHA256; match bundled native payload hashes to native/manifest.json and verify expected adapter resources exist in the bundle.
Run deploy-performance.py without --apply and preserve its concrete target list before the authorized installation step.
After apply, require manifest status=applied and verify each target against afterSha256; preserve the rollback directory.
After a normal desktop restart, confirm the actual executable path/version, native persistence activation, session search behavior and helper disposal using the parent runtime checks.
Verify native-disabled and unsupported-kernel paths retain official session access. Compare original session data/config using the parent baseline evidence.
Review native cache integrity using the queries in data-migrations.json when needed; never run migration or cleanup against authoritative logs.
rollback: Require manifest status=rolled-back and confirm all restored targets equal beforeSha256, with originally absent files absent.
If interruption occurs, rerun rollback with the same manifest. Do not remove retained images or alter journal entries to bypass ownership/hash failures.

A currently loaded newly installed addon or executable may keep its running process on the new implementation until normal exit. Verify restored behavior only after normal restart; do not stop the user's process as part of this review.
Cache schema rollback is unnecessary for official operation because the cache is disposable and original logs are not rewritten.

reviewed: native-helper/src/index.rs opens only desktop-text-v1.sqlite under the independently owned cache directory; runtime.mjs selects DSH_HOME/cache/desktop-native.

Legacy rows map session, seq, text and folded unchanged, with part=0 and preview=NULL. BEGIN IMMEDIATE covers rename, copy, drop, default-backed quota columns, backfill and LRU index creation; migration errors roll back.
Cache eviction and suffix replacement commit atomically with revision comparison. Search revision validation and result selection share one SQLite snapshot, including empty results.
Existing migration, quota, disk-full and two-helper tests were inspected; previously reported passing tests were not rerun.
verification_queries: SELECT d.session FROM documents d LEFT JOIN sessions s USING(session) WHERE s.session IS NULL LIMIT 1;
SELECT s.session FROM sessions s WHERE s.documents <> (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT seq) FROM documents d WHERE d.session=s.session) LIMIT 1;
SELECT session,seq FROM documents GROUP BY session,seq HAVING MIN(part)<>0 OR MAX(part)+1<>COUNT(*) LIMIT 1;
notes.query_caveat: Run optional integrity queries only against the derived cache; quick_check should return ok and invariant queries should return no rows. Do not mutate or migrate official logs or official index databases.

residual_risks: Native activation is deliberately fail-closed on platform, version, or artifact mismatch; in that state the desktop_session_search tool is absent even though official session functionality remains available. This is an operational capability boundary rather than a parity defect in the shipped compatible path.

The activation gate pins the CLI plus session and persistence packages, while desktop-native-tools also imports dsh-session-query and cordis APIs without checking their package versions. The current locked 0.1.2-rc.1 bundle provides the expected APIs, but a selectively modified installation under the same CLI version would rely on fail-safe plugin load behavior rather than an explicit compatibility gate.

Kernel compatibility version 0.1.2-rc.1 is repeated independently in desktop/native/activation.js, persistence.mjs, session-text.mjs, and scripts/deploy-performance.py. The checks currently agree, but an official-kernel upgrade requires coordinated edits across activation, fallback, and deployment paths; a shared generated compatibility manifest would reduce drift.

The native helper protocol number is duplicated between Rust and two JavaScript transports. Current values all equal 1, but there is no single generated contract or mandatory handshake in NativeClient, so a future partial upgrade could fail only after the first real operation.
Successful loaded-image replacement retains `.before-native-*` sibling binaries with no cleanup path; this is bounded per deployment but can accumulate across repeated upgrades.

Rollback trusts any manifest located beneath install/repair-checks; an accidentally selected or locally modified manifest can operate on allowed install/plugin targets, although hash checks limit ordinary stale-manifest damage.

The document-key migration is forward-only inside disposable desktop-native cache. Returning to a helper that expects the legacy document shape may require retiring that derived cache with all helper processes stopped; authoritative session logs remain untouched and official fallback remains available.

Replacing a loaded Windows executable changes the next launch; the current process continues using its retained image. Activation and rollback therefore require verification after a normal restart, without terminating a user session.
Rollback intentionally refuses foreign edits and tampered backups. Preserve the manifest, byte backups and journal-owned retained images until recovery and post-restart verification are complete.
The migration journal supports process interruption, but its writes are not explicitly fsync-backed; sudden power loss durability was not established by the inspected interruption tests.
testing_gaps: The reviewed tests exercise traversal and request/slice bounds, but do not cover Windows junction/reparse-point containment or a second-session argument attempting to override desktop_session_search's caller-derived scope. Static inspection found both boundaries enforced; this leaf pass did not execute additional tests.

The scoped-query finding is independently validated, but its fix should include a targeted query-plan/result check against bundled SQLite 3.46.0; this review executed system SQLite 3.45.3 and inspected the bundled planner source.

Final source-to-built-artifact hashes, NSIS bundle inspection, actual installation and post-restart runtime evidence remain pending with the parent release workflow. These are release evidence gates, not asserted code defects.
